The first public release of **Lictor**: keep an eye on every terminal and coding agent in [Herdr](https://herdr.dev/), without touching them.

![A Lictor mirror tab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyscallBrain/lictor/main/docs/src/images/mirror.png)

## Highlights

- **Focus rotation:** cycle Herdr's focus through workspaces, tabs, panes and agents, mixed in any order, with status filters (`--status blocked,done`), repeat entries and shuffling.
- **Live split mirrors:** `lictor -W -A -s 5 -S w,a` opens a new tab with two read-only lanes that rotate on their own. Workspace mirrors rebuild the whole source layout, and every mirror keeps the newest output in view.
- **Keyboard controller:** run `lictor` for a Vim-style TUI in Tokyo Night. Build either mode on a two-lane board, then start, pause and stop jobs from its Jobs panel.
- **Managed jobs:** rotations run detached. `--jobs`, `--pause`, `--resume`, `--stop` and `--close-view` control them from anywhere.
- **Safe by design:** Lictor never sends input to your agents, never moves or resizes panes, and only closes tabs it created.

## Install

Download `lictor-0.1.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz` below, check it against `SHA256SUMS`, and put `lictor` on your `PATH`:

```bash
tar -xzf lictor-0.1.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz
install -m 755 lictor-0.1.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/lictor ~/.local/bin/
```

Or build it with Cargo:

```bash
cargo install --git https://github.com/SyscallBrain/lictor --tag v0.1.0 --locked
```

## Requirements

- Linux x86_64
- A running Herdr session; tested with Herdr 0.9.3. Split mirrors also need `herdr` in `PATH`.
- Optional: `notify-send` for notifications, and tmux or X11 + `xdotool` for sidebar control.

## Known limitations

- Linux only for now.
- Mirrors are read-only, and the Herdr 0.9.3 observer doesn't forward inline (Kitty) images.
- A source bigger than its mirror is cropped; the source terminal is never resized.

📖 Read [the Lictor book](https://syscallbrain.github.io/lictor/) to get started.
